verses.zh: （大卫的诗。）耶和华是我的亮光，是我的拯救，我还怕谁呢？耶和华是我性命的保障（或译：力量），我还惧谁呢？
verses.en: By David.The Lord is my light[NOTE:1] and my salvation.I fear no one.[NOTE:2] The Lord protects my life.I am afraid of no one.[NOTE:3]
notes: Psalm 27. The author is confident of the Lord’s protection and asks the Lord to vindicate him.

“Light” is often used as a metaphor for deliverance and the life/blessings it brings. See Pss 37:6; 97:11; 112:4; Isa 49:6; 51:4; Mic 7:8. Another option is that “light” refers here to divine guidance (see Ps 43:3).
Heb “Whom shall I fear?” The rhetorical question anticipates the answer, “No one.”

verses.zh: 那作恶的就是我的仇敌，前来吃我肉的时候就绊跌仆倒。
verses.en: When evil men attack me[NOTE:1] to devour my flesh,[NOTE:2] when my adversaries and enemies attack me,[NOTE:3] they stumble and fall.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “Of whom shall I be afraid?” The rhetorical question anticipates the answer, “No one!”
Heb “draw near to me.”
To devour my flesh. The psalmist compares his enemies to dangerous, hungry predators (see 2 Kgs 9:36; Ezek 39:17).
Heb “my adversaries and my enemies against me.” The verb “draw near” (that is, “attack”) is understood by ellipsis; see the previous line.

verses.zh: 虽有军兵安营攻击我，我的心也不害怕；虽然兴起刀兵攻击我，我必仍旧安稳。
verses.en: Even when an army is deployed against me,I do not fear.[NOTE:1] Even when war is imminent,[NOTE:2] I remain confident.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew verbal forms are perfects. The translation assumes the psalmist is generalizing here, but another option is to take this as a report of past experience, “when evil men attacked me…they stumbled and fell.”
Heb “my heart does not fear.”
Heb “if war rises up against me.”

verses.zh: 有一件事，我曾求耶和华，我仍要寻求：就是一生一世住在耶和华的殿中，瞻仰他的荣美，在他的殿里求问。
verses.en: I have asked the Lord for one thing—this is what I desire!I want to live[NOTE:1] in the Lord’s house[NOTE:2] all the days of my life,so I can gaze at the splendor[NOTE:3] of the Lordand contemplate in his temple.
notes: Heb “in this [i.e., “during this situation”] I am trusting.”
Heb “for me to live.”
The Lord’s house. This probably refers to the tabernacle (if one accepts Davidic authorship) or the temple (see Judg 19:18; 1 Sam 1:7, 24; 2 Sam 12:20; 1 Kgs 7:12, 40, 45, 51).

verses.zh: 因为我遭遇患难，他必暗暗地保守我；在他亭子里，把我藏在他帐幕的隐密处，将我高举在磐石上。
verses.en: He will surely[NOTE:1] give me shelter[NOTE:2] in the day of danger;[NOTE:3] he will hide me in his home.[NOTE:4] He will place me[NOTE:5] on an inaccessible rocky summit.[NOTE:6]
notes: Or “beauty.”
Or “for he will.” The translation assumes the כִּי (ki) is asseverative here, rather than causal.
Heb “he will hide me in his hut.”
Or “trouble.”
Heb “tent.”
The three imperfect verb forms in v. 5 anticipate a positive response to the prayer offered in vv. 7-12.

verses.zh: 现在我得以昂首，高过四面的仇敌。我要在他的帐幕里欢然献祭；我要唱诗歌颂耶和华。
verses.en: Now I will triumphover my enemies who surround me.[NOTE:1] I will offer sacrifices in his dwelling place and shout for joy.[NOTE:2] I will sing praises to the Lord.
notes: Heb “on a rocky summit he lifts me up.” The Lord places the psalmist in an inaccessible place where his enemies cannot reach him. See Ps 18:2.

In vv. 1-3 the psalmist generalizes, but here we discover that he is facing a crisis and is under attack from enemies (see vv. 11-12).tn Heb “and now my head will be lifted up over my enemies all around me.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，我用声音呼吁的时候，求你垂听；并求你怜恤我，应允我。
verses.en: Hear me,[NOTE:1] O Lord, when I cry out.Have mercy on me and answer me.
notes: Heb “I will sacrifice in his tent sacrifices of a shout for joy” (that is, “sacrifices accompanied by a joyful shout”).

verses.zh: 你说：你们当寻求我的面。那时我心向你说：耶和华啊，你的面我正要寻求。
verses.en: My heart tells me to pray to you,[NOTE:1] and I do pray to you, O Lord.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “my voice.”

Heb “concerning you my heart says, ‘Seek my face.’” The verb form “seek” is plural, but this makes no sense here, for the psalmist is addressed. The verb should be emended to a singular form. The first person pronominal suffix on “face” also makes little sense, unless it is the voice of the Lord he hears. His “heart” is viewed as speaking, however, so it is better to emend the form to פָּנָיו (panayv, “his face”).

verses.zh: 不要向我掩面。不要发怒赶逐仆人，你向来是帮助我的。救我的　神啊，不要丢掉我，也不要离弃我。
verses.en: Do not reject me.[NOTE:1] Do not push your servant away in anger.You are my deliverer.[NOTE:2] Do not forsake or abandon me,O God who vindicates me.
notes: Heb “your face, O Lord, I seek.” To “seek the Lord’s face” means to seek his favor through prayer (see 2 Sam 21:1; Pss 24:6; 105:4).
Heb “do not hide your face from me.” The idiom “hide the face” can mean “ignore” (see Pss 10:11; 13:1; 51:9) or carry the stronger idea of “reject” (see Pss 30:7; 88:14).

verses.zh: 我父母离弃我，耶和华必收留我。
verses.en: Even if my father and mother abandoned me,[NOTE:1] the Lord would take me in.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “[source of] help.”
Or “though my father and mother have abandoned me.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你将你的道指教我，因我仇敌的缘故引导我走平坦的路。
verses.en: Teach me how you want me to live,[NOTE:1] Lord; lead me along a level path[NOTE:2] because of those who wait to ambush me.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “gather me in”; or “receive me.”
Heb “teach me your way.” The Lord’s “way” refers here to the moral principles which he expects the psalmist to follow. See Ps 25:4.
The level path refers to God’s moral principles (see the parallel line), which, if followed, will keep the psalmist blameless before his accusers (see v. 12).

verses.zh: 求你不要把我交给敌人，遂其所愿；因为妄作见证的和口吐凶言的，起来攻击我。
verses.en: Do not turn me over to my enemies,[NOTE:1] for false witnesses who want to destroy me testify against me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “because of those who watch me [with evil intent].” See also Pss 5:8; 54:5; 56:2.
Heb “do not give me over to the desire of my enemies.”

verses.zh: 我若不信在活人之地得见耶和华的恩惠，就早已丧胆了。
verses.en: Where would I be if I did not believe I would experiencethe Lord’s favor in the land of the living?[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for they have risen up against me, lying witnesses and a testifier of violence.” The form יָפֵחַ (yafeakh) is traditionally understood as a verb meaning “snort, breathe out”: “for false witnesses are risen up against me, and such as breathe out cruelty” (KJV; cf. BDB 422 s.v.). A better option is to take the form as a noun meaning “a witness” (or “testifier”). See Prov 6:19; 12:17; 14:5, 25; 19:5, 9, and Hab 2:3.

verses.zh: 要等候耶和华！当壮胆，坚固你的心！我再说，要等候耶和华！
verses.en: Rely[NOTE:1] on the Lord!Be strong and confident![NOTE:2] Rely on the Lord!
notes: In the Hebrew text the sentence is incomplete: “If I had not believed [I would] see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living.” The words “Where would I be” are supplied in the translation to clarify the intent of the statement.
Or “wait.”
